transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (PolyNimbus PM), Sara Al-Mansouri (Tech Lead), Lena Ortiz (Partner Eng)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Discussed marketplace listing steps, reference arch for private deployments, billing integration and SSO. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for making time, this is Alex from Redwood, I think we've got the right people from PolyNimbus, Ravi, Sara, Lena you on?
[00:12] Ravi: Yep, hi Alex, thanks. Sara and Lena are here. Good to meet you Maya, Jordan.
[00:18] Maya: Hi all. Quick note we dumped a draft of the marketplace listing in the shared drive — link in the calendar note, but we'll walk through the fields.
[00:28] Sara: Great, our PM wants a clear reference arch for customers who want a private deployment behind our VPC marketplace offering.
[00:36] Jordan: Cool, we can show two patterns — SaaS hosted integration and private, where customers subscribe via PolyNimbus and deploy Redwood in their VPC or on-prem.
[00:48] Ravi: Main questions from our side: what artifacts do you need for listing, what installer or image do we publish, and how does billing work when a customer buys via PolyNimbus?
[01:02] Alex: Good. On artifacts — we need marketing copy, logos, plan definitions, support SLAs, and an AMI or container image and an installation manifest for the private flow. For hosted flow it's mostly an integration webhook and redirect info.
[01:22] Sara: For private we require a reference architecture diagram, network flow showing VPC peering or transit gateway, and guidance on KMS/HSM if customers need to bring keys. Also SOC2 evidence is asked by our compliance gate.
[01:38] Maya: We can provide a reference arch doc that maps to Redwood Private — includes KMS integration options (customer-managed keys), SSO via SAML, and audit logs. Note the transcription might say "K V cash" sometimes in older notes, it's K V cache — sorry for the auto transcript noise.
[01:56] Ravi: (laughs) yeah the transcript bots do that. On billing — PolyNimbus expects a metering API from vendors, we need usage callbacks or invoice CSVs. Can Redwood push per-customer usage records?
[02:12] Jordan: Yes, Redwood has a billing export API; we can provide daily usage CSVs or push events. We typically support per-token and embedding units, but for marketplace use we can map to a single SKU and send aggregated usage if you prefer.
[02:30] Sara: Aggregated is easier for our billing flow but we'll need mapping details. Also what's your plan for version pinning — e.g., customers may want to pin a model or rollout policies. How to represent that in the marketplace?
[02:46] Alex: Good point. We represent versioning in the listing metadata — you can declare default model and list compatible variants. For private images we include a reference to the specific image tag. For Hosted we allow customers to set a model_version parameter.
[03:05] Ravi: Competitors like CloudMart have a quick onboarding flow that asks for an OIDC client and SCIM. Does Redwood support SCIM for user provisioning?
[03:18] Maya: We do. SCIM and SAML both supported. Small caveat: for on-prem installs customers manage their SSO endpoint; for hosted we integrate with your IdP via SAML/SCIM. We'll document required attributes.
[03:34] Sara: Ok. On the reference architecture — can we go through the VPC peering scenario? We need to show the egress rules, NAT, and where the KV cache sits.
[03:46] Jordan: Sure. For Private VPC flow, the Redwood control plane can be either a customer-controlled control plane or a lightweight connector. Data plane (inference nodes) lives in the customer's subnet, with KMS calls routed to the customer's KMS. The KV cache (sometimes transcript writes K V cash) is a local in-memory/redis layer; we recommend a managed Redis or our built-in caching depending on scale.
[04:12] Ravi: For our marketplace listing we typically require a reference arch PNG and a text doc ~1-2 pages. Can you deliver that?
[04:20] Maya: Yes, we'll send a one-page diagram and a 2-page technical brief. Jordan will own the diagram.
[04:26] Jordan: Yep I'll take that.
[04:30] [09:01] Sara: Quick question about network egress costs — if Redwood images call back to your hosted control plane, will customers see more egress?
[09:10] Alex: We optimize to minimize callbacks; control plane interactions are small. However, model weights and updates are pulled initially — we can chunk that and provide a checksum. For marketplace private installs we can also provide an image that includes the weights so no large download on install.
[09:36] Ravi: Nice. On security/compliance — our procurement asks for SOC2, ISO certs, and vulnerability scan reports. Do you have links?
[09:46] Maya: Yes, we have a SOC2 report and a whitepaper on our security controls. We'll share the redacted SOC2 and an uptime SLAs doc.
[09:55] Lena: Also want to confirm audit logs — we need to ingest or fetch customer audit logs for actions and tokens.
[10:02] Jordan: We can forward audit logs to an S3 bucket or stream them to your syslog/ELK. We'll include examples in the doc.
[10:12] Ravi: For billing integration, PolyNimbus supports two patterns: marketplace-mediated billing where we bill the customer and settle with vendors via monthly statements, or pass-through where vendors bill directly. Which do you prefer?
[10:26] Alex: We can do either. Marketplace-mediated is simplest for PolyNimbus customers, but requires us to provide usage exports in your schema. Pass-through is simpler for us but might complicate customer UX. We'll match whichever works best — suggest we start marketplace-mediated for first launch.
[10:42] Sara: We'll need a sample payload and an auth model for your billing export. Prefer signed webhooks with an HMAC.
[10:50] Jordan: HMAC webhooks are supported. We can also provide SFTP drop for CSV. We'll attach sample docs.
[11:00] [19:30] Ravi: What about trial/free tier provisioning — do you have a plan to provision trial tenant via API so we can issue trial entitlements?
[19:40] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports trial tokens and provisioning via API; we can generate a trial SKU tied to the marketplace order ID. We'll document flow and permission scoping.
[19:55] Alex: Also include rate limits and burst policies in the listing — customers ask about QPS and latency SLOs.
[20:04] Sara: Right, typical customers want 99th percentile latency guarantees for interactive apps. Do you have numbers for your hosted endpoints and for dedicated pools?
[20:14] Jordan: For hosted we publish median latencies by model; dedicated pools have predictable throughput with per-tenant SLOs. We'll share a performance profile sheet. Note the numbers depend on sequence length and batching.
[20:28] Ravi: Any caveats about quantized models? Some customers are sensitive to model quality regression when switching to int8.
[20:36] Maya: We'll provide recommended quantization profiles per workload and quality regression tests. We'll flag tradeoffs in the doc.
[20:46] Alex: Great. On operations: onboarding support — we usually include 30 days of dedicated onboarding support for marketplace-launched customers. Is that acceptable?
[20:55] Ravi: Yes, that fits. We also want a runbook for common issues (permissions, network).
[21:02] Jordan: We'll include a runbook and sample firewall rules.
[21:06] [28:10] Lena: For the listing page we need three screenshots and a short 150-word description plus feature bullets. Who is owning the marketing copy?
[28:18] Alex: Marketing owns copy, but we'll draft the 150-word description and send it to Ravi for edits.
[28:25] Ravi: Sounds good. Please put the draft in the shared doc and we'll iterate.
[28:30] Maya: Noted. We'll also provide the logos in SVG and PNG.
[28:34] Sara: One more technical deep dive item — how do you handle model rollbacks if a new release causes regressions for a customer?
[28:43] Jordan: We support pinning to model variants and can roll back on a per-tenant basis. We keep model artifacts versioned and can restore prior weights. We'll document the rollback playbook.
[28:54] Ravi: Good.
[29:00] [37:50] Alex: Ok recap and next steps: Maya to send ref arch + perf profile (due 2026-05-27), Jordan to produce image/upload instructions and diagram (due 2026-05-29), Alex will draft marketplace listing copy and send to Ravi by 2026-05-25, Ravi to share onboarding checklist by 2026-05-26.
[38:10] Sara: We'll also set up a staging tenant on PolyNimbus side for the integration test; propose we schedule the staging test week of June 1.
[38:22] Jordan: Works for us, we'll be ready to upload image and run a compatibility check.
[38:30] Ravi: Any blockers?
[38:34] Alex: Only blocker is missing SOC2 redaction; we'll send that doc via your secure share.
[38:40] Maya: Also need confirmation on billing fields and schema — Ravi if you can send that JSON schema we'll map fields.
[38:47] Ravi: I'll send the billing schema and a sample order payload after this call.
[38:52] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[38:56] Lena: One small thing — for the marketplace listing we sometimes require legal contact and partner terms. Who handles partner agreements?
[39:04] Alex: Our legal team handles partner terms; I'll introduce you to our legal ops in the follow-up email.
[39:12] Ravi: Perfect.
[39:15] [46:30] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and action items. Look forward to the staging run.
[46:38] Ravi: Thanks all, talk soon.
[46:41] End of transcript.
